## 固定收益開篇論點

6月24日收盤時，前一交易日集中於前端的紓壓行情，已擴展為美債中段領漲。10年期殖利率收於4.41%，下跌9個基點，實質殖利率與通膨補償同步下降。能源價格下跌仍是最明確的催化劑：通過荷姆茲海峽的船舶增加，區域出口逐步恢復，美國與伊朗談判取得進展，削弱戰時供給溢價長期存在的理由。因此，美債反映的是通膨路徑改善，並不需要以成長預期崩潰為前提。

相較6月23日，主要變化在殖利率曲線與漲勢構成。週二的牛市趨陡反映市場質疑聯準會下次升息的時點，但長端仍受偏高實質殖利率牽制。週三轉為牛市趨平，5年至30年期殖利率跌幅均大於2年期。實質殖利率沿整條曲線下滑，顯示行情已不再局限於通膨避險成本下降。房市數據不如預期，增添美國內需降溫訊號；5年期公債標售順利，也顯示大額附息公債供給能被市場消化，未中斷漲勢。

這波行情由3條管道推動。第一，航運逐步正常化，其影響蓋過美國原油庫存大幅減少，帶動原油期貨下跌約4%，並降低能源對損益兩平通膨率的貢獻。第二，聯準會定價由擔憂立即升息，轉向升息急迫性下降、但政策仍具限制性的路徑，使5年期券相對領漲。第三，美債供給獲得足夠的最終投資人需求，讓漲勢得以延續；極短期國庫券殖利率維持穩定，也不支持現金市場同步吃緊的看法。

反向力量來自美元走強，以及若干重要經濟體的政策立場仍偏鷹。歐洲央行官員持續表示可能需要進一步緊縮，日本央行也重申，剛調升至1%的政策利率可能仍須上調。信用市場同樣維持篩選：投資級債受惠於較長存續期間與美債上漲，但較低評級債券基金幾乎持平，承壓借款人仍須採用股權連結、利息實物支付或延長到期日等結構。此次收盤確實代表存續期間紓壓範圍擴大，但實質殖利率仍具限制性，海外利率形成競爭，個別借款人也面臨再融資壓力，因此行情仍有條件。

## 美債利率、聯準會定價、實質殖利率與殖利率曲線結構

漲勢以中段最強。2年期殖利率下跌5個基點至4.11%，5年期下跌10個基點至4.17%，30年期則下跌8個基點至4.86%。5年期券相對領漲，扭轉本週稍早的弱勢；此前，政策不確定性、附息公債供給與企業利率避險，使賣壓集中於該區段。長債也跟進上漲，但幅度較小，顯示市場仍要求較高補償，以承擔較遠期的財政與供給風險。

殖利率曲線指標反映行情由週二的牛市趨陡轉為週三的牛市趨平。2年期與10年期利差收窄4個基點至30個基點，2年期與30年期利差收窄3個基點至75個基點。5年期券相對曲線兩端走強，使2s5s10s蝶式利差下降6個基點至負18個基點。2s10s30s蝶式利差下降5個基點至負15個基點，顯示10年期券的表現也優於前端與長端的平均。這代表資金沿曲線延長存續期間，而不只是立即升息疑慮消退後的反彈。

通膨連結債券定價顯示，名目公債漲勢的構成相對均衡。10年期實質殖利率下跌6個基點至2.23%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點至2.18%。5年期與7年期實質殖利率分別下跌5個及6個基點，至1.98%與2.09%；20年期下跌6個基點至2.53%，30年期下降5個基點至2.71%。通膨補償下降只能解釋部分行情，投資人也願意接受各年期較低的實質報酬。

能源是最直接的通膨傳導管道。美國與伊朗釋出和平談判有所進展的訊號後，通過荷姆茲海峽的油輪增加，儘管協商仍未定案。6月初，阿拉伯聯合大公國石油出口已恢復至戰前水準的近85%；卡達則預期，未受損的液化天然氣產能可在數週內恢復正常。這些進展降低實體供應長期中斷的機率，也減輕運費、燃料及生產成本長期居高不下的風險。

美國成長數據在邊際上也指向降溫。5月新屋銷售不如預期，建築許可亦弱於市場預估，進一步顯示利率敏感部門正在降溫。這些資料尚不足以證明經濟步入衰退；2年期殖利率跌幅較小，也顯示投資人並未排除聯準會進一步緊縮。不過，數據確實降低市場因能源通膨而押注聯準會立即採取行動的必要性，並協助漲勢由損益兩平通膨率延伸至實質存續期間。

$700億的5年期公債標售是附息券需求的核心事件。新券最高得標殖利率為4.200%，票面利率為4又1/8%，投標倍數為2.35。間接投標人承接$430.28億，直接投標人承接$178.20億，初級交易商則獲配競爭性得標中的$90.06億。由於標售結果未提供發行前交易殖利率作為比較，主要訊號來自投標倍數與分配結構：美債中段上漲之際，這筆大額標售仍吸引最終投資人大量參與。

較短期供給也順利消化，未顯示融資市場普遍承壓。$280億浮動利率債券增額發行的投標倍數為2.99，最高折價利差為0.079%，利差為0.103%。間接投標人承接競爭性得標中的$186.50億，交易商承接$93.31億，直接投標人未獲配。$690億的119天期國庫券標售，最高折價率為3.770%，相當於3.871%的投資收益率，投標倍數為2.55。間接投標人獲配$374.14億，高於交易商的$284.95億。

現金券殖利率依到期年限呈現差異。4週、6週、8週與13週期券的附息券等值殖利率分別維持在3.62%、3.69%、3.72%與3.79%。17週期殖利率上升2個基點至3.87%，與標售所測試的區間一致；26週與52週期殖利率則分別下降1個及2個基點，至3.94%與3.98%。浮動利率債券於6月26日交割；119天期國庫券與5年期公債於6月30日交割。這些未來現金移轉與當日投標結果是兩件事，不能據此認定當天已出現交割壓力。

市場結構仍是有序標售背後的主要風險。一名聯準會經濟學家估計，截至2025年9月，以附買回交易融資的現券與期貨基差交易達$8,300億，占避險基金美債多頭曝險的35%。美債總曝險從2023年9月至2025年9月倍增至$4兆，其中規模最大的50檔基金掌握90%。這類槓桿在正常環境下可支撐流動性，但也使風險高度集中；一旦波動率或保證金出現衝擊，套利部位平倉可能演變為被迫收縮資產負債表。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

信用市場明顯分化為利率存續期間與較低評級信用風險。美債殖利率下跌帶動LQD上漲0.4591%，HYG小跌0.0250%，JNK下跌0.0623%。投資級債券基金因存續期間較長，總報酬表現較佳。投機級債券基金接近平盤，顯示利率行情未轉化為全面的信用風險漲勢；不過，兩檔基金的表現也未顯示融資市場普遍退潮。

紐約聯準銀行6月公司債市場壓力指數支持市場運作有序的判斷。整體市場指標月內改善，月底略高於歷史第20百分位。投資級債市場運作約處於歷史第50百分位，高收益債市場壓力則維持歷史低檔。該指數同時衡量初級市場發行與定價、次級市場流動性，以及有成交與無成交債券，因此指數改善代表整體市場運作正常，即使個別發行人的融資條件差異仍相當顯著。

總發行量進一步確認，市場運作正常並非只靠少數交易支撐。6月美國投資級債發行量達$1,750億，較2025年6月全月高60%，並超越2020年創下的月度紀錄；Nvidia與SpaceX各發行$250億，而交易商原先預估全月約為$1,300億。年初至今供給達$1.15兆，與2020年同期相當。緊俏的信用利差抵銷較高的基準殖利率，市場預期聯準會可能升息，也促使發行人提早鎖定資金；6月發行量可能超過$2,000億。龐大發行量證明市場承接能力，但也加深投資人對AI相關資本支出的集中曝險。

大型策略性借款人仍能取得深厚資金。SpaceX已完成$250億首次發債，證明投資級債投資人有能力承接與再融資及AI支出相關的超大型交易。後續籌資案仍相當龐大：NTT正準備約$100億多幣別債券發行；ByteDance則考慮約$200億境外貸款，同時評估今年投入最高$700億的AI相關支出。這些計畫尚未確定最終定價或投資人需求，因此是下一輪市場承接能力的考驗，不能視為已完成吸收。

企業也透過不同資本工具為AI投資週期籌資。SK Hynix計畫發行在Nasdaq上市的存託憑證，籌集45.45兆韓元，約合$294億，預計7月10日開始交易。股權融資可降低債券市場資產負債表短期內的承接需求，但整體支出熱潮仍會增加未來借款、電力基礎設施與執行需求。債券、貸款及股權籌資案同步增加，顯示充裕的融資管道集中於資本密集產業。

在龐大發行日程之下，投資人持續沿流動性光譜承擔更多風險。使用Clearwater Analytics的企業財務主管，其投資組合持有Rule 144A債券的中位數比重為2%，高於數年前接近零的水準。相較可比的公開發行投資級債，平均殖利率溢價約為52個基點。這項統計涵蓋逾400家公司，管理資產約$1兆，顯示即使以現金管理為主的買方，也願意犧牲部分流動性以換取額外殖利率。

Hertz說明信用較弱的借款人如何透過融資結構付出代價。這家汽車租賃公司計畫發行$3億可轉換利息實物支付票券，並搭配$1億股票，供可轉債投資人建立空頭部位。公司部分循環信貸額度將於6月到期，而利息實物支付條款可避免立即支付現金票息。公司警告第2季調整後獲利不會超過$8,000萬後，股價下跌41%。融資管道仍然存在，但較弱發行人必須接受股權稀釋、占用優先受償空間及遞延利息，無法取得較強發行人享有的單純融資條件。

印度Shapoorji Pallonji Group則呈現同一信用分化下的到期管理問題。該集團提出支付30個基點同意費，將1,430億盧比零息債券的到期日至少延後1個月，超過6月30日。另一項相關請求擬將Porteast Investment的一項債務條件延至9月；此前，一筆$34億貸款的貸款價值比上限已暫時由34%提高至40%。這些借款以該集團持有的Tata Sons 18.4%股權作為擔保，因此抵押品價值下跌正直接壓縮再融資彈性。

歷史定價顯示，抵押品與執行風險已相當嚴峻。Goswami的零息債券於2023年以18.75%殖利率定價，當時是印度規模最大的高收益債發行；其未償本金後來降至834.2億盧比，殖利率卻升至21.75%。Porteast另一筆$34億借款以19.75%定價，債權人包括Ares、Cerberus、Davidson Kempner、Farallon及Deutsche Bank。多數貸款人支持展期，但Ares仍在協商，因此30個基點同意費本身不足以證明所有債權人均接受再融資安排。

整體而言，信用市場在系統層面仍具流動性，但對個別借款人的待遇明顯分化。投資級債受惠於較長存續期間與美債上漲，大型科技相關融資依然可行，市場運作指標也有所改善。追逐殖利率的需求已延伸至流動性較低的證券。然而，高收益債總報酬並未跟上投資級債漲勢，承壓借款人仍須採用保留現金或延後償付的結構。融資管道持續開放，但融資條件透露的訊息比總發行量更重要。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

油價下跌減輕歐洲眼前的通膨衝擊，卻未促使政策轉向鴿派。歐洲央行執行委員Isabel Schnabel表示，若要使通膨回到2%，可能仍須進一步升息，幅度與時點將取決於衝突、經濟成長及物價。她強調能源價格仍高於戰前水準，遠期能源成本也依舊偏高。歐洲央行總裁Christine Lagarde認為無須採取更強力的措施，因此政策討論仍聚焦於再度審慎升息，而非緊急加速緊縮。

成長環境讓歐洲央行有空間審慎行事。德國ifo商業景氣指數由5月的85.0升至6月的85.6。企業對當前情勢的評估改善，對未來的看法也較不悲觀；但即使預期轉強，製造業訂單仍再次下降。服務業、貿易與營建業也僅呈現不均衡改善。數據降低短期衰退風險，卻未顯示經濟強勁復甦；這種組合限制德國公債的上漲空間，同時使其仍容易受到能源成本傳導影響。

日本的政策正常化傾向更為明確。日本央行6月會議摘要指出，金融環境仍然寬鬆，基礎通膨接近2%，因此支持繼續升息。此前，日本央行以7比1決議將政策利率調升至1%，為1995年以來最高。一名委員認為中性利率約為2%，位於央行估計的1.1%至2.5%區間內；另一名委員主張，可考慮每隔數月採取一次行動。日本央行總裁Kazuo Ueda也警告通膨可能超過目標，並表示緊縮步調將取決於經濟、物價及金融情勢。

匯率傳導使日本央行的訊息不只影響日本。即使升息，日圓仍接近數十年低點，輸入性通膨與匯率干預風險因此持續受到關注。日本政策利率與公債殖利率上升，會提高保險公司、銀行及退休基金的國內投資報酬門檻，並改變日本公債與匯率避險後美債的相對吸引力。影響雖然漸進，卻限制美債存續期間行情在海外買方結構不變的假設下持續延伸。

澳洲的政策反應則相近但不完全相同。澳洲央行副總裁Andrew Hauser認為，經濟已移至菲利浦曲線較陡峭的區段，因此快速緊縮可能以較小的就業代價降低通膨。澳洲央行在今年前3次會議均升息後，將政策利率暫停於4.35%，同時保留再次緊縮的選項。央行預測通膨要到2028年年中才會回到2%至3%目標區間的中點，失業率則將在4.7%見頂。

南韓則因金融穩定風險，使區域利率底部維持偏高。南韓央行自2025年下半年以來將政策利率維持在2.5%，並表示隨首爾地區房價、家庭債務及槓桿投資再度累積金融失衡，應在適當時點提高利率。銀行與非銀行金融機構仍保有符合監管要求的資本與流動性緩衝，因此央行並非認定系統正面臨立即壓力。風險主要集中於脆弱借款人、非銀行金融機構流動性，以及以槓桿融資的資產購買。總體審慎政策因而只能配合未來升息，不能取代貨幣政策緊縮。

加拿大面臨相反的成長限制，政策選擇卻同樣不容易。實質GDP在第1季年化萎縮0.1%，前一季則下滑1%；但超過半數產業仍在擴張，消費支出也上升，因此決策者認為疲弱程度既不深也不廣，尚不足以構成衰退。加拿大央行將政策利率維持在2.25%，核心通膨指標接近2%，能源價格傳導也有限。政策風險並不對稱：如果油價已正常化後才升息，緊縮可能沒有必要；但若等待期間能源成本持續傳導，日後可能被迫採取幅度更大的升息。

歐洲財政規則也為期限溢價增添限制。歐盟允許成員國運用原為國防支出設計的豁免條款，進行有限的能源韌性投資，但仍維持3%的赤字上限及各國特定支出路徑。信評分析師將這項彈性視為範圍有限的應變措施，而非信用紀律破口；不過，買方結構仍然重要。2026年全球主權借款預估達$14.1兆，歐洲央行正在縮減持債，荷蘭退休基金也在降低長天期曝險。即使目前的彈性未觸發信評行動，若例外一再增加，約束財政紀律的責任仍會逐步轉向債券投資人。

全球存續期間走勢仍不同步，但共同的利率底部依然偏高。德國經濟展現溫和韌性，歐洲央行仍考慮再次升息，日本央行表示將進一步推動政策正常化，澳洲央行也強調暫停升息附帶條件。油價下跌緩解各央行眼前的通膨問題，但沒有任何一家央行認為能源價格回落已足以恢復寬鬆政策。這也說明美債雖在6月24日強勁上漲，市場卻未因此認定全球限制性實質利率已經告終。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

儘管匯率環境略為收緊，新興市場美元債仍受惠於美債殖利率下降。EMB上漲0.3220%，美元指數則上升0.1972%至101.61。EMB取得正總報酬，顯示整體而言，美債基準殖利率下降帶來的存續期間利多，超過美元當日走強的不利影響。各國表現則遠為分歧，因能否取得融資仍取決於外匯存底、國內融資成本，以及各項負債操作的法律結構。

阿根廷利用替代融資管道，建立近期償債能力。政府須於7月9日支付$42億債券款項，目前已累積約$36億財政部美元存款，足以支付約85%的款項。經濟部長Luis Caputo籌集硬通貨的平均成本為6.7%，低於目前透過國際市場融資約9%的成本，也低於數月前約10%的水準。其他資金則來自本地美元債券發行、央行購匯及多邊機構支持的融資。

短期成本下降並未消除中期再融資風險。阿根廷發行2027年及2028年到期的本地美元債券，也透過國內標售以接近20%的固定利率吸收披索，實質利率約為7%。另一項法令授權政府借入最多$50億美元，由世界銀行及美洲開發銀行等機構提供支持，估計成本接近6%。國家風險已降至430個基點附近，至少較先前低100個基點，使市場重新評估阿根廷何時能以合算的成本恢復國際發債。

墨西哥通膨數據改善近期政策取捨。6月上半月消費者物價年增3.55%，低於調查預估中位數3.72%。核心通膨降至4.12%，接近4.13%的預估，顯示低於預期主要來自非核心項目。政策利率目前為6.50%，央行並將2026年經濟成長預測由1.6%下調至1.1%。整體通膨壓力減弱，支持央行耐心觀望；但核心通膨仍具黏著性，尚不能解讀為明確的寬鬆訊號。

中國製造業產能過剩，為新興市場本幣債提供結構性支撐。貿易壁壘促使更多中國出口轉向開發中經濟體，價格較低的商品可抑制當地通膨，讓央行擁有更多降息空間。Pimco結合這項通膨降溫管道、新興市場相對較高的實質殖利率及正統政策框架，看好拉丁美洲，尤其是巴西、哥倫比亞與秘魯。不過，這項觀點並非普遍適用：中國的生產與消費缺口可改善進口國通膨，卻也會加重當地產業競爭壓力；美元走強仍可能蓋過本地利率的利多。

智利與印度顯示，能源價格下跌可以改變本地利率路徑，卻無法消除國內風險。燃料成本大幅上漲使通膨超過目標後，智利將政策利率維持在4.5%；5月物價月增0.2%，僅為調查預估幅度的一半，官員仍預測通膨將於2027年第2季回到3%。印度10年期公債殖利率下跌5個基點至6.82%，因印度央行總裁表示，現在討論升息仍為時過早；不過，截至6月22日，季風降雨短缺43%，食品通膨風險仍未消除。

整體而言，新興市場近期流動性改善，但再融資條件仍高度分化。油價下跌有利能源進口國，美債上漲也支撐硬通貨債券報酬。阿根廷透過存款與信用增強融資管道降低7月付款風險；墨西哥獲得維持利率不變的空間；智利與印度升息的急迫性也有所下降。不過，美元堅挺、國內融資成本偏高，以及未來到期債務仍待處理，將決定短期紓壓能否轉化為持久的主權融資管道。

## 跨資產

美股並未出現足以完全解釋美債漲勢的全面避險行情。S&P 500小跌0.0983%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.4335%，費城半導體指數下跌0.1803%。VIX下降4.4125%至18.63。科技股集中度及財報公布前的審慎情緒拖累股市，但波動率下降，顯示投資人並未大幅提高系統性風險避險成本。

油價提供利率行情最有力的跨資產佐證。WTI下跌3.9202%至$70.34，Brent下跌4.3332%至$73.74；兩者近1個月跌幅分別達27.1843%與28.7812%。油價跌幅大且延續時間長，加上實體航運狀況改善，支持通膨補償下滑。這也使美債上漲能與風險市場穩定並存：主要驅動因素是投入成本衝擊緩解，而非市場預期需求崩潰。

美國能源資訊署庫存報告使供應稀缺的判斷更為複雜，但未推翻油價下跌的主線。商業原油庫存減少610萬桶至4.121億桶，較5年同期平均低約7%。汽油庫存增加210萬桶，蒸餾油庫存增加310萬桶，煉油產能利用率達96.1%。過去4週汽油需求較去年同期低3.0%，即使總石油產品供應量增加2.1%。成品油庫存增加、汽油需求轉弱，使市場得以淡化原油庫存大減的影響。

美元與貴金屬仍反映實質利率具有限制性。美元指數收於101.61，近1週漲幅擴大至1.5186%；黃金下跌3.3802%至$3,990.30。美元走強及市場對聯準會的偏鷹預期也壓抑金屬價格，銅價下跌1.9%至每噸$13,117.50。美債上漲同時伴隨美元走強與黃金走弱，符合能源通膨降溫、實質殖利率從高檔回落的情境，而非全球流動性重新轉為充裕。

跨資產走勢因而將通膨降溫與經濟衰退區隔開來。油價、黃金與損益兩平通膨率同步下跌，股市小幅回落卻未引發波動率飆升。美元仍受美國相對政策立場支撐，投資級債報酬也比投機級債更佳。這種組合支持受控的存續期間漲勢：行情由能源價格正常化及政策時點調整推動，尚未顯示信用環境或成長預期已全面惡化。

## 市場前瞻意義

6月25日08:30 ET公布的美國數據，包括5月PCE通膨、個人所得與支出、耐久財訂單、第1季GDP第3次估值及初領失業救濟金人數，將共同檢驗存續期間漲勢能否擴大。若基礎物價壓力的廣度趨緩，支出同時放慢或勞動市場進一步降溫，將確認油價下跌正在影響政策預期，而且沒有需求激增加以抵銷；2年至10年期實質殖利率曲線與短期聯準會利率定價將最為敏感。若核心通膨堅挺、消費維持韌性，或商品價格壓力再起，週三由損益兩平通膨率延伸至實質殖利率的行情將受到挑戰，中段實質利率底部可能抬高，市場也會重新認為紓壓主要集中於前端。若數據好壞參半，5年期標售的承接訊號仍然成立，但下次升息時點將繼續存在不確定性。

6月25日的美債供給將檢驗週三中段的相對強勢，能否承受另一波大額發行。$700億4週期與$750億8週期國庫券將於11:30 ET標售，隨後是13:00的$440億7年期公債標售，以及13:40至14:00的20年至30年期名目附息公債買回；各項標售均於6月30日交割。若投標倍數強勁、直接與間接投標人廣泛參與、交易商獲配比例維持低檔，且現金國庫券殖利率穩定，將確認5年期標售反映持久的資產負債表承接能力，並可能延續牛市趨平。若7年期公債需求疲弱、交易商獲配過度集中，或6月30日現金移轉前後出現壓力，供給可有序消化的論點將受到挑戰，中段可能重新出現新券讓利，市場也會再度檢視槓桿美債部位的融資風險。

美國收盤後，全球政策利率底部將面臨3項檢驗。歐洲央行經濟公報預定於6月25日10:00 CEST發布；墨西哥央行將於15:00 ET公布利率決議，目前隔夜利率為6.50%；6月東京消費者物價指數初值則於6月26日08:30 JST公布。若歐洲能源成本傳導正在消退、墨西哥維持利率不變且匯率壓力受控，以及日本通膨擴散程度轉弱，將確認即使美元維持堅挺，油價下跌仍能減輕各市場維持限制性政策的競爭。若歐元區第2輪通膨壓力持續、墨西哥央行指引偏鷹，或東京通膨再度升溫，德國公債與日本公債殖利率、美元及新興市場再融資成本都可能上升，使美債存續期間繼續面對較高的海外市場出清利率。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The June 24 close broadened the prior session’s narrow front-end relief into a rally led by the Treasury belly. The 10-year yield finished at 4.41%, 9 basis points lower, as both real yields and inflation compensation declined. Cheaper energy remained the clearest catalyst: more vessels were moving through the Strait of Hormuz, regional exports were recovering, and progress in US-Iran talks weakened the case for a persistent wartime supply premium. Treasuries therefore responded to an improving inflation path without requiring a collapse in growth expectations.

The change from June 23 was in the curve and the composition of the rally. Tuesday’s bull steepening had questioned the timing of the next Fed increase while leaving the long end constrained by elevated real yields. Wednesday produced a bull flattening, with 5- through 30-year yields falling more than the 2-year. Real yields declined across the curve, so the move was no longer confined to cheaper inflation protection. Disappointing housing indicators added a domestic cooling signal, and the successful 5-year auction showed that a large coupon offering could clear without interrupting the rally.

3 channels carried the move. Oil futures fell roughly 4% as shipping normalization competed successfully with a sizable US crude-inventory draw. That lowered the energy contribution to breakevens. The Fed channel shifted from immediate-hike anxiety toward a less urgent, still-restrictive path, allowing the 5-year sector to outperform. Treasury supply then met enough end-investor demand to keep the rally intact, while stable very-short bill yields argued against a concurrent cash squeeze.

The counterforce was a firmer dollar and an international policy map that remained hawkish in important places. ECB officials continued to describe further tightening as likely, and the BOJ reiterated that its new 1% policy rate may need to rise again. Credit also remained selective: high-grade duration benefited from Treasuries, yet lower-quality funds were nearly flat and stressed borrowers still required equity-linked, payment-in-kind or maturity-extension structures. The close marks a genuine expansion of duration relief, but the combination of restrictive real yields, foreign rate competition and idiosyncratic refinancing pressure keeps it conditional.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The rally was strongest around the belly. The 2-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.11%, the 5-year dropped 10 basis points to 4.17%, and the 30-year declined 8 basis points to 4.86%. 5-year outperformance reversed its relative weakness earlier in the week, when policy uncertainty, coupon supply and corporate-rate hedging had concentrated pressure in that sector. The long bond participated, but its smaller move preserved a higher compensation hurdle for distant fiscal and supply risk.

Curve measures captured the shift from Tuesday’s bull steepening to Wednesday’s bull flattening. The 2s10s spread narrowed 4 basis points to 30, and 2s30s narrowed 3 to 75. The 2s5s10s butterfly fell 6 basis points to -18 as the 5-year richened against both wings. The 2s10s30s butterfly declined 5 basis points to -15, showing that the 10-year also outperformed the average of the front and long ends. The move was a duration extension, not simply a reversal of immediate policy fear.

Inflation-linked pricing gave the nominal rally a balanced composition. The 10-year real yield fell 6 basis points to 2.23%, while the 10-year breakeven declined 3 basis points to 2.18%. 5- and 7-year real yields dropped 5 and 6 basis points to 1.98% and 2.09%. The 20-year real yield fell 6 basis points to 2.53%, and the 30-year declined 5 to 2.71%. Lower inflation compensation explained only part of the move; investors also accepted less real return across maturities.

Energy supplied the most direct inflation transmission. More tankers crossed Hormuz as the United States and Iran signaled progress in peace talks, even though negotiations remained unsettled. UAE oil exports had recovered to nearly 85% of prewar levels in early June, and Qatar expected undamaged LNG capacity to return to normal within weeks. Those developments weakened the probability that disrupted physical supply would keep freight, fuel and production costs elevated for an extended period.

The domestic growth signal pushed in the same direction at the margin. May new-home sales disappointed and building permits were weaker than expected, adding evidence of interest-sensitive cooling. The information was not broad enough to establish a downturn, and the smaller decline in the 2-year yield showed that investors had not abandoned the prospect of further Fed restraint. It did, however, reduce the need to price an immediate response to energy inflation and helped move the rally beyond breakevens into real duration.

The $70 billion 5-year auction was the central coupon-demand event. The new note stopped at a 4.200% high yield with a 4-1/8% coupon and a 2.35 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders accepted $43.028 billion and direct bidders $17.820 billion, leaving primary dealers with $9.006 billion of the competitive award. With no when-issued comparison attached to the result, the useful signal came from coverage and distribution: the large sale found substantial end-buyer participation as the belly rallied.

Shorter supply also cleared without a common funding shock. The $28 billion floating-rate-note reopening drew a 2.99 bid-to-cover ratio at a 0.079% high discount margin and a 0.103% spread. Indirect bidders took $18.650 billion of the competitive award, dealers $9.331 billion and direct bidders none. The $69 billion 119-day bill sale stopped at a 3.770% high discount rate, equivalent to a 3.871% investment rate, with 2.55 bid-to-cover. Indirect awards of $37.414 billion exceeded the dealer allocation of $28.495 billion.

Cash yields remained differentiated by maturity. 4-, 6-, 8- and 13-week coupon-equivalent yields were unchanged at 3.62%, 3.69%, 3.72% and 3.79%. The 17-week yield rose 2 basis points to 3.87%, matching the area tested by the auction, while 26- and 52-week yields fell 1 and 2 basis points to 3.94% and 3.98%. The FRN settles June 26; the 119-day bill and 5-year note settle June 30. Those future cash transfers are distinct from the bidding results and did not create same-day evidence of settlement pressure.

Market structure remains the principal qualification to the orderly auction picture. A Federal Reserve economist estimated that the repo-financed cash-futures basis trade accounted for $830 billion, or 35%, of hedge funds’ long Treasury exposure as of September 2025. Gross Treasury exposure doubled between September 2023 and September 2025 to $4 trillion, and the 50 largest funds controlled 90% of the total. This leverage can support liquidity in normal conditions, yet it also concentrates the risk that a volatility or margin shock turns arbitrage unwinds into forced balance-sheet contraction.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Credit performance divided cleanly between rate duration and lower-quality risk. LQD gained 0.4591% as Treasury yields fell, while HYG slipped 0.0250% and JNK declined 0.0623%. The high-grade fund’s stronger total return was compatible with its greater duration exposure. The near-flat speculative-grade results showed that the rates rally did not become a broad credit-risk rally, but neither fund move indicated a general retreat from financing.

The New York Fed’s June Corporate Bond Market Distress Index supported an orderly-functioning interpretation. The market-level measure improved during the month and ended slightly above its historical 20th percentile. Investment-grade functioning finished around its historical 50th percentile, and high-yield distress remained historically low. Because the index combines primary issuance and pricing with secondary liquidity and traded-versus-nontraded bond measures, its improvement indicates broad market operation even as individual issuers faced sharply different economics.

Aggregate issuance confirmed that the functioning signal was not confined to a few deals. June U.S. investment-grade sales reached $175 billion, 60% above all of June 2025 and above the previous monthly record set in 2020; Nvidia and SpaceX contributed $25 billion each, versus dealers’ roughly $130 billion forecast for the month. Year-to-date supply reached $1.15 trillion, matching the comparable 2020 pace. Tight spreads helped offset higher benchmarks, while prospective Fed increases encouraged issuers to lock funding early; the volume could exceed $200 billion. The same strength that demonstrated capacity also deepened investors’ concentration in AI-linked capital spending.

Large strategic borrowers still had access to deep pools of capital. The completed $25 billion SpaceX debut sale confirmed that high-grade investors could absorb an exceptional transaction linked to refinancing and AI spending. The new pipeline remained substantial: NTT was preparing a roughly $10 billion multi-currency bond sale, and ByteDance was considering an offshore loan of about $20 billion while weighing as much as $70 billion of AI-related expenditure this year. These plans had not yet established final pricing or demand, so they define the next capacity test rather than completed absorption.

Companies were also diversifying the form of capital used to fund the AI cycle. SK Hynix planned to raise 45.45 trillion won, or $29.4 billion, through Nasdaq-listed depositary receipts, with trading expected to begin July 10. Equity funding can reduce the immediate call on bond-market balance sheets, though the broader spending boom still raises future borrowing, power-infrastructure and execution needs. The simultaneous debt, loan and equity pipelines show abundant access concentrated around a capital-intensive sector.

Demand beneath the headline calendar continued to move outward along the liquidity spectrum. The median corporate treasurer using Clearwater Analytics held 2% of its portfolio in Rule 144A bonds, up from close to zero several years earlier. The average yield premium over a comparable publicly held high-grade bond was about 52 basis points. The shift, measured across more than 400 companies with roughly $1 trillion under management, shows that even cash-focused buyers were accepting less liquidity to capture additional yield.

Hertz illustrated how weaker borrowers paid for access through structure. The car-rental company paired a planned $300 million convertible payment-in-kind note with $100 million of stock intended to be shorted by convertible investors. Part of its revolving facility expires in June, and the PIK feature avoids an immediate cash coupon. The shares fell 41% after the company warned that Q2 adjusted earnings would be no more than $80 million. Financing remained possible, but dilution, seniority capacity and deferred interest replaced the straightforward economics available to stronger issuers.

India’s Shapoorji Pallonji Group supplied a maturity-management version of the same dispersion. It offered a 30-basis-point consent fee to extend 143 billion rupees of zero-coupon bonds by at least 1 month beyond June 30. A related request would extend a debt condition at Porteast Investment to September after the loan-to-value cap on a $3.4 billion loan had temporarily risen to 40% from 34%. The borrowings are backed by the group’s 18.4% stake in Tata Sons, so falling collateral value is directly tightening refinancing flexibility.

The pricing history showed how severe that collateral and execution risk had
become. Goswami's zero-coupon notes originally priced at an 18.75% yield in
2023, then India's largest high-yield sale, and the outstanding principal had
fallen to 83.42 billion rupees while the yield rose to 21.75%. Porteast's
separate $3.4 billion borrowing had priced at 19.75% and was held by creditors
including Ares, Cerberus, Davidson Kempner, Farallon, and Deutsche Bank. Most
lenders supported the requested extensions, but Ares was still negotiating,
so the 30-basis-point consent fee did not by itself establish unanimous
refinancing capacity.

The credit tape was therefore liquid at the system level and discriminating at the borrower level. High-grade duration benefited from the Treasury rally, large technology-linked financing remained feasible, and market-functioning indicators improved. Search-for-yield demand extended into less-liquid securities. Yet high-yield total returns did not join the high-grade advance, and stressed credits needed structures that preserve cash or postpone repayment. Open access persists, with terms carrying more information than aggregate volume.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Lower oil reduced the immediate inflation shock in Europe without producing a dovish policy turn. ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said further increases would probably be needed to return inflation to 2%, with the scale and timing dependent on the conflict, growth and prices. She emphasized that energy prices remained above prewar levels and that forward energy costs were still elevated. President Christine Lagarde saw no need for a more forceful response, leaving the debate centered on another measured move rather than an emergency acceleration.

The growth backdrop gave the ECB room to proceed cautiously. Germany’s ifo Business Climate Index rose to 85.6 in June from 85.0 in May. Current-condition assessments improved and expectations became less skeptical, but manufacturing orders declined again even as expectations strengthened. Services, trade and construction also improved unevenly. The result reduced immediate recession risk without describing a forceful recovery, a combination that limits Bund rally potential while preserving sensitivity to energy pass-through.

Japan maintained a clearer normalization bias. The BOJ’s June meeting summary said accommodative financial conditions and underlying inflation near 2% supported continued increases, following the 7-1 decision to lift the policy rate to 1%, its highest since 1995. 1 member placed neutral around 2%, within the bank’s broader estimated range of 1.1% to 2.5%, and another favored considering moves at intervals of a few months. Governor Kazuo Ueda also warned that inflation could exceed target and linked the pace of tightening to economic, price and financial conditions.

Currency transmission keeps that message relevant beyond Japan. The yen remained close to multi-decade weakness even after the rate increase, leaving imported inflation and intervention risk in focus. Higher Japanese policy and sovereign yields raise the domestic return hurdle for insurers, banks and pensions that compare JGBs with hedged Treasuries. The effect is gradual, but it limits how far a US duration rally can rely on an unchanged foreign buyer base.

Australia offered a related but distinct reaction function. Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser argued that rapid tightening could lower inflation with a smaller employment cost because the economy had moved onto a steeper part of the Phillips curve. The RBA paused at 4.35% after increases at its first 3 meetings of the year, while retaining the option to tighten again. Its forecasts put inflation back at the midpoint of the 2%-3% target only in mid-2028, with unemployment peaking at 4.7%.

South Korea added a financial-stability reason to keep the regional rate floor high. The Bank of Korea, which has held its policy rate at 2.5% since the second half of 2025, said a higher rate would be needed at an appropriate time as Seoul-area home prices, household debt and leveraged investment rebuilt financial imbalances. Banks and nonbanks retained regulatory capital and liquidity buffers, so this was not a claim of immediate system stress. The risk instead lay in vulnerable borrowers, nonbank liquidity and asset purchases financed with leverage, making macroprudential coordination a complement to eventual policy tightening rather than a substitute for it.

Canada faced the opposite growth constraint without obtaining an easy policy answer. Real GDP contracted at a 0.1% annualized rate in Q1 after a 1% decline in Q4, but more than half of industries expanded, consumer spending rose and policymakers judged the weakness neither deep nor broad enough to constitute recession. The Bank of Canada held at 2.25% with core measures near 2% and limited energy pass-through. Its dilemma remained asymmetric: tightening after oil had already normalized could be unnecessary, while waiting through persistent pass-through could force more aggressive increases later.

European fiscal rules supplied another term-premium qualification. The EU allowed limited energy-resilience investment under an escape clause originally designed for defense, while preserving the 3% deficit ceiling and country-specific expenditure paths. Ratings analysts treated the flexibility as a bounded response rather than a credit rupture, but the buyer-base context matters: global sovereign borrowing was projected at $14.1 trillion in 2026, the ECB was shrinking holdings, and Dutch pensions were reducing long-duration exposure. Repeated exceptions would shift enforcement toward bond investors even if the current accommodation did not trigger rating action.

Global duration remained asynchronous, yet the common floor stayed high. Germany showed modest growth resilience, the ECB kept another increase in view, the BOJ described further normalization, and the RBA framed its pause as conditional. Falling oil softened each central bank’s immediate inflation problem, but none treated the energy reversal as sufficient to restore easy policy. That backdrop explains why Treasuries could rally strongly on June 24 without turning the move into a global declaration that restrictive real rates had ended.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market dollar debt gained from lower Treasury yields even as the currency backdrop tightened slightly. EMB rose 0.3220%, while the US Dollar Index added 0.1972% to 101.61. The fund’s positive total return shows that benchmark-duration relief outweighed the daily dollar headwind at the broad level. Country outcomes remained far more dispersed because access depended on reserves, domestic funding costs and the legal structure of each liability operation.

Argentina converted alternative funding into near-term payment capacity. The government must meet a $4.2 billion bond payment on July 9 and had accumulated about $3.6 billion in Treasury dollar deposits, enough for roughly 85% of the obligation. Economy Minister Luis Caputo assembled hard currency at an average cost of 6.7%, compared with roughly 9% for a current international-market transaction and about 10% several months earlier. Local dollar placements, central-bank purchases and multilateral-backed financing supplied the remaining channels.

The lower immediate cost did not eliminate medium-term refinancing risk. Argentina issued local dollar bonds maturing in 2027 and 2028 and also captured pesos through domestic auctions at fixed rates near 20%, or real rates around 7%. A decree separately authorized as much as $5 billion of dollar borrowing backed by institutions including the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank, with an estimated cost near 6%. Country risk had fallen into the 430-basis-point area, at least 100 basis points below earlier levels, reopening the question of when global issuance becomes economical.

Mexico’s inflation release improved the near-term policy trade-off. Consumer prices rose 3.55% from a year earlier in H1 of June, below the 3.72% median survey estimate. Core inflation eased to 4.12%, close to the 4.13% estimate, so the upside surprise was concentrated outside the underlying measure. With the policy rate at 6.50% and the central bank’s 2026 growth forecast reduced to 1.1% from 1.6%, weaker headline pressure supports patience while sticky core inflation prevents a simple easing signal.

China’s excess manufacturing capacity offered a structural counterweight for local-currency emerging-market debt. As trade barriers redirected more Chinese exports toward developing economies, cheaper goods could restrain inflation and leave central banks with more room to cut. Pimco paired that disinflation channel with relatively high EM real yields and orthodox policy frameworks, favoring Latin America, particularly Brazil, Colombia and Peru. The view is conditional rather than universal: the production-consumption gap can improve importer inflation while intensifying competitive pressure on domestic industry, and a stronger dollar can still overwhelm the local-rate benefit.

Chile and India showed how cheaper energy affected local-rate paths without removing domestic risks. Chile kept its policy rate at 4.5% after a major fuel-cost increase had pushed inflation above target; May prices rose 0.2% on the month, half the surveyed pace, and officials still projected a return to 3% inflation in Q2 of 2027. India’s 10-year government yield fell 5 basis points to 6.82% after the RBI governor called hike discussion premature, though a monsoon deficit of 43% through June 22 preserved a food-inflation contingency.

The EM conclusion is improving near-term liquidity with persistent refinancing differentiation. Lower oil helped importers, and the Treasury rally supported hard-currency bond returns. Argentina reduced a July payment risk through deposits and credit-enhanced channels; Mexico gained room to hold policy; Chile and India saw less urgency to tighten. A firm dollar, costly domestic funding and unresolved future maturities still determine whether that relief becomes durable sovereign access.

## Cross asset

US equities did not deliver the kind of broad risk-off move that would fully explain the Treasury rally. The S&P 500 slipped 0.0983%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.4335% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 0.1803%. The VIX declined 4.4125% to 18.63. Technology concentration and pre-earnings caution weighed on stocks, but falling volatility indicated that investors were not paying sharply more for systemic protection.

Oil provided the strongest cross-asset confirmation of the rates move. WTI fell 3.9202% to $70.34 and Brent dropped 4.3332% to $73.74. Their 1-month declines reached 27.1843% and 28.7812%. The scale and persistence of the fall supported lower inflation compensation, especially as physical shipping conditions improved. It also made the Treasury rally compatible with stable risk markets: the dominant impulse was relief from an input-cost shock, not a collapse in expected demand.

The EIA inventory release complicated the scarcity picture without overturning it. Commercial crude stocks fell 6.1 million barrels to 412.1 million, about 7% below the 5-year seasonal average. Gasoline stocks rose 2.1 million barrels and distillates increased 3.1 million, while refinery utilization reached 96.1%. 4-week gasoline demand was 3.0% below its year-earlier rate even as total products supplied rose 2.1%. Product builds and softer gasoline demand helped markets look through the crude draw.

The dollar and precious metals preserved the restrictive real-rate signal. The Dollar Index closed at 101.61, extending its 1-week gain to 1.5186%, while gold fell 3.3802% to $3,990.30. Copper also declined 1.9% to $13,117.50 a ton as a stronger dollar and hawkish Fed expectations weighed on metals. A Treasury rally alongside a firmer dollar and weaker gold is consistent with reduced energy inflation and lower real yields from elevated levels, not a return to globally abundant liquidity.

Cross assets therefore separated disinflation from recession. Oil, gold and breakevens fell together, and modest equity losses did not generate a volatility spike. The dollar remained supported by the relative US policy stance, while high-grade bond returns benefited more than speculative-grade risk. That configuration strengthens the interpretation of a controlled duration rally driven by energy normalization and policy timing, with no broad signal that credit or growth expectations had broken.

## Forward Market Significance

The June 25 US release block at 08:30 ET brings May PCE inflation, personal income and spending, durable-goods orders, the 3rd estimate of Q1 GDP and initial claims into 1 test of the broader duration rally. Softer underlying price breadth alongside slower spending or further labor cooling would confirm that lower oil is reaching policy expectations without a compensating demand surge; the most sensitive channels would be the 2- to 10-year real-yield curve and short-dated Fed pricing. Firm core inflation, resilient consumption or renewed goods-price pressure would challenge Wednesday’s move beyond breakevens, lift the belly’s real-rate floor and reopen the prior interpretation that relief belongs mainly at the front end. A mixed result would leave the 5-year auction’s absorption signal intact but keep the timing of the next policy increase unsettled.

Treasury supply on June 25 tests whether Wednesday’s belly outperformance can survive another heavy sequence. The $70 billion 4-week and $75 billion 8-week bill auctions arrive at 11:30 ET, followed by a $44 billion 7-year note at 13:00 and a 20- to 30-year nominal-coupon buyback from 13:40 to 14:00; the auctions settle June 30. Strong coverage, broad direct and indirect participation, contained dealer awards and stable cash-bill yields would confirm that the 5-year result reflected durable balance-sheet capacity and could extend the bull flattening. Weak 7-year demand, a concentrated dealer allocation or pressure around the June 30 cash transfer would challenge the orderly-supply thesis, push concession back into the belly and reopen funding scrutiny around leveraged Treasury positions.

The global policy floor receives a 3-part check after the US close. The ECB Economic Bulletin is due June 25 at 10:00 CEST, Banxico decides at 15:00 ET with its overnight rate currently at 6.50%, and preliminary June Tokyo CPI arrives at 08:30 JST on June 26. Evidence that European energy pass-through is fading, a steady Mexican rate with contained currency pressure, and softer Japanese inflation breadth would confirm that lower oil can reduce cross-market competition for restrictive policy even when the dollar remains firm. Persistent euro-area second-round pressure, hawkish Banxico guidance or renewed Tokyo inflation would challenge that interpretation through Bund and JGB yields, the dollar and EM refinancing costs, preserving a higher foreign clearing rate for US duration.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury belly leads broader rally as energy normalization eases inflation pressure
overall_summary.session_narrative: At the June 24 NY close, the 5- through 30-year sectors outperformed the 2-year as lower oil, softer housing signals and reduced urgency around Fed tightening pulled down both real yields and breakevens. Strong 5-year auction participation and a record $175 billion June high-grade calendar showed deep absorption. The move stopped short of broad easing because Korea’s financial-stability risks, Canada’s energy dilemma, European fiscal flexibility and a firmer dollar kept global clearing rates and credit differentiation relevant.
overall_summary.summary: Cheaper energy and softer housing data extended Treasury relief from the front end into real duration, while strong 5-year auction demand preserved the move. Record high-grade issuance showed capacity, but a firmer dollar, hawkish foreign central banks and selective borrower terms kept the rally conditional.
